title: Lexical Tone and Word Order Matter in Translation: Prosodic Correspondence Across Languages
abstract: arXiv:2611.31276v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Prosody conveys emphasis, emotion, and intent, yet its correspondence across translation remains underexplored, especially when languages differ in lexical tone and word order. To our knowledge, we present the first systematic word-level analysis of prosodic correspondence in translated speech spanning tonal and non-tonal Asian languages, with comparisons to European-language findings and explicit analyses of lexical tone and word reordering. Building on prior evidence of fine-grained prosody correspondence in European-language pairs, we investigate how these linguistic factors relate to word-level pitch and energy correspondence between English and five languages: Mandarin Chinese, Thai, and Vietnamese, which have lexical tone, and Japanese and Korean as additional comparisons. Correspondence is generally lower than previously reported European-language estimates. Adjusting for lexical tone increases pitch correspondence for English-Man

translated_title: 声调与词序在翻译中至关重要：跨语言的韵律对应性研究
translated_abstract: 韵律传达着强调、情感和意图，但其在翻译中的对应关系仍未得到充分探索，尤其是当语言之间在声调和词序上存在差异时。据我们所知，我们首次对翻译语音中的韵律对应性进行了系统的词级分析，涵盖声调与非声调的亚洲语言，并与欧洲语言的研究结果进行比较，同时显式分析声调和词序重排的影响。基于先前关于欧洲语言对之间细粒度韵律对应性的证据，我们研究了这些语言因素如何影响英语与五种语言之间的词级音高和能量对应关系，这五种语言包括具有声调的普通话、泰语和越南语，以及作为额外比较的日语和韩语。研究结果显示，韵律对应性总体上低于先前报告的欧洲语言估计值；调整声调因素后，英语与普通话之间的音高对应性有所提升。
tldr: 该研究首次对跨越声调与非声调亚洲语言的翻译语音进行了词级韵律对应性系统分析，发现声调和词序显著影响翻译中的韵律对应程度，且其对应水平总体低于先前报告的欧洲语言对的结果。
en_tdlr: This study presents the first systematic word-level analysis of prosodic correspondence in translated speech across tonal and non-tonal Asian languages, showing that lexical tone and word order significantly shape prosodic correspondence, which is generally lower than previously reported for European language pairs.
